questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A) As the day ended, the sky turned orange and pink, painting a beautiful picture above the peaceful park.

B) Children ran and laughed, playing games on the green grass.

C) Their families sat on colourful blankets, enjoying picnics in the sunshine.

D) The park was big and full of trees and flowers.
questions.solution_en: The logical sequence to form a coherent paragraph is DBCA. Sentence D provides the initial description, setting the scene by describing the park's size and its natural elements. Sentence B follows the description of the park and introduces the activity of children playing games on the grass, adding movement and liveliness to the scene. Sentence C logically follows, describing their ('children' mentioned in sentence B) families taking advantage of the pleasant setting to enjoy picnics in the park. Sentence A introduces the sunset scene, concluding the sequence by setting the atmosphere as the day comes to an end with a picturesque sky over the serene park. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hi: The logical sequence to form a coherent paragraph is DBCA. Sentence D provides the initial description, setting the scene by describing the park's size and its natural elements. Sentence B follows the description of the park and introduces the activity of children playing games on the grass, adding movement and liveliness to the scene. Sentence C logically follows, describing their ('children' mentioned in sentence B) families taking advantage of the pleasant setting to enjoy picnics in the park. Sentence A introduces the sunset scene, concluding the sequence by setting the atmosphere as the day comes to an end with a picturesque sky over the serene park. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. As with any doppelgangers, their friends know the difference between them, their mothers probably couldn't even see the resemblance.

B. Llamas (Lama glama) and alpacas (Lama pacos) are like those two people you see around town all the time who look just alike.

C. To be fair, llamas and alpacas, both herd animals, are so closely related they can interbreed and create fertile offspring, so their strong resemblance is no surprise.

D. But to the average human, both of these pack animals, kind of resemble an ostrich mixed with a standard poodle and a camel, which is a really specific look.
questions.solution_en:
The correct order is BADC.

Sentence B comes first as it is an independent sentence and provides a platform to carry forward the discussion. Sentence B states that the appearance of Llamas and alpacas is the same. A follows B as it is the continuation of B. The noun 'doppelganger(s)' means 'a spirit that looks exactly like a living person'. Sentence A states that the close ones cannot see the similarity between the doppelgangers. 'But' is used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned. D follows A as it conveys that we humans cannot easily identify the difference between these two animals. The remaining sentence C is the last part of the passage.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

A woman was selling oranges. We were buying some of them from the woman.
options_en: Oranges were being sold by a woman. Some of them were being bought by us from the woman.
Oranges are being sold by the woman. Some of them are being bought by us from the woman.
Oranges were being sold by a woman. Some of them was bought by us from the woman.
Oranges have been sold by a woman. Some of them have been bought by us from the woman.
questions.solution_en:
In a passive voice sentence, the subject in the given active voice sentence becomes the object in the passive voice sentence and the object in an active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.

The tense remains the same in both the active and passive voice sentences and in the passive voice sentence the doer of the action is denoted with the help of the preposition 'by'.

The format of a passive voice sentence is: Subject + Verb + by + Object.

In the active voice, the tense is Past continuous which remains the same in the passive voice too.

In options (b) and (d), the tense of the passive voice sentences is 'Present continuous' and 'Present Perfect tense', respectively, so they are negated. In option (c), the verb 'was' in the second sentence is incorrect as the verb corresponds to a singular noun, but 'some' is a plural pronoun. So, option (c) is also negated.

Option (a) 'Oranges were being sold by a woman. Some of them were being bought by us from the woman' is the correct form of the passive voice sentence, which follows the required grammatical norms of a passive voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in superlative degree of comparison.

He works harder than anyone else in his office.
options_en: He works hardest in his office.
Harder worker in his office is he.
No one else in his office works as hard as he does.
He works hard in his office.
questions.solution_en:
The adverb is 'hard' and it is in the comparative degree, which means it compares one thing or person with another and shows that it has a higher or lower degree of quality. To change a sentence from the comparative degree to the superlative degree, we need to add -est to an adverb. The superlative degree shows that something or someone has the highest degree of quality among all the others in a group.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Option (b) is incoherent.

Options (c) and (d) are in positive degree.

Note:

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

One's family plays a very major role to continue the trends and age-old traditions.
options_en: passive role in making the trends
significant role in enduring the trends
questions.solution_en:
In the underlined phrase the verb 'to continue' is in infinite form, but the sentence implies that the action to follow age-old traditions still continues and so the verb has to be in the continuous form of the verb (V4). Among the given options, in option (a), 'passive role' contradicts the context of the given sentence as the sentence indicates an active continuation of following the tradition and thus it is negated. Also, age-old traditions cannot be made in the present, they are already there. In options (b) and (d), 'futile' (incapable of producing any useful result; pointless) and 'docile' (ready to accept control or instruction; submissive) are contextually irrelevant words and thus they cannot replace the given incorrect phrase. Thus, options (b) and (d) are also negated. Option (c) 'significant role in enduring the trends' is the most appropriate option that can replace the incorrect phrase given in the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Chefs and food scientists can manipulate cooking conditions to achieve optimal flavour and appearance by understanding the principles behind this complex process.

B. It is this very process that is responsible for producing the desirable brown colour and the savoury flavours in foods like seared steaks and toasted bread.

C. The Maillard reaction, a form of non-enzymatic browning, occurs when amino acids and reducing sugars in food are subjected to high heat.

D. This chemical transformation not only changes the food's appearance but also creates hundreds of new aroma compounds that enhance its overall taste profile.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence is CBDA. Sentence C introduces the scientific term "The Maillard reaction" and explains the basic conditions under which it occurs, making it the most logical starting point. Sentence B directly refers to the reaction mentioned in C with the phrase "It is this very process," and explains its most noticeable results (browning and flavour). Sentence D then elaborates on "This chemical transformation," providing more detail about the creation of new aroma compounds. Finally, sentence A concludes the paragraph by discussing the practical application, explaining how "Chefs and food scientists" use their understanding of "this complex process" to improve cooking.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a helping verb [being] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is in interrogative form. These are "wh" questions that don't take "yes" or "no" as an answer.

For example:

What are you doing? (Active)

What is being done by you? (Passive)

Also, the sentence is in the Present Continuous tense in the Active voice. So, in the Passive voice, Present Continuous tense should be used.

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is: (a) What is being considered by Ancelloti about the tactics of Real Madrid before the final match against Barcelona at the Camp Nou?

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Once upon a time, in a grand estate perched on a hill, there lived an arrogant woman named Victoria. Victoria had recently married a wealthy widower, becoming the stepmother to his young son, Thomas. Her arrival brought an air of entitlement and superiority that cast a shadow over their once happy home. Victoria saw Thomas as an obstacle to her new life of luxury. She resented his presence, considering him an inconvenience that stood in the way of her ambitions. Thomas, despite his tender age, possessed a resilient spirit. He yearned for his father's love and acceptance, but Victoria's coldness only incited his determination to rise above her contemptuous behaviour. He sought solace in his own imagination, finding refuge in books and daydreams that transported him far away from the reality of their toxic household.

Victoria's arrogance began to crumble as she witnessed the positive impact Thomas had on others. She saw his unwavering kindness and the light he brought into their home. Slowly, her heart softened, and she realized the error of her ways. Regret filled her as she reflected on the years of mistreatment and the missed opportunities to build a genuine bond with Thomas. In a moment of vulnerability, Victoria approached Thomas, seeking forgiveness for her past actions. With tears in her eyes, she expressed her remorse and acknowledged the hurt she had caused. Thomas, in a display of grace beyond his years, embraced her with forgiveness, understanding that everyone deserves a chance to change.

From that day forward, Victoria and Thomas worked to rebuild their relationship. Their story became a testament to the transformative power of humility and forgiveness. Victoria learned that true strength lies not in arrogance, but in the ability to acknowledge one's mistakes and grow from them. And Thomas, through his resilience and capacity for forgiveness, showed that love can prevail, even in the face of adversity. In the end, their journey together taught them both valuable lessons about the importance of compassion, empathy, and the capacity for change.

Which term can be used to describe Victoria's initial behaviour?
questions.solution_en:
'Haughty' means arrogantly superior and disdainful. It is distinctly mentioned in the first paragraph of the passage that she was an arrogant woman so 'haughty' is the right word here.

'Resilient' means strong.

'Courteous' means polite and respectful.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

All member of this / old age home actively / participates in the marathons / conducted by the state.
questions.solution_en:
A pronoun must agree with its antecedent in person, number, and gender. The noun following 'all' is 'member' which is singular in nature. And 'all' refers to a complete group of people/things (plural in nature).

So, instead of 'all', 'every' fits in the sentence as it refers to each member of the group individually (singular in nature).

This means 'all' in the given sentence makes it grammatically incorrect.

Replace it with 'every' to rectify the error.

Correct sentence: Every member of this old age home actively participates in the marathons conducted by the state.

So, option b) is the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Hence, option b) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that is the direct form of the given sentence.

Brinda told her doctor that she was leaving for Boston the next day.
options_en: Brinda told to her doctor, "I will be leaving for Boston the next day".
Brinda told her doctor, "I was leaving for Boston tomorrow".
Brinda said to her doctor, "I am leaving for Boston tomorrow."
Brinda had told her doctor, "She was leaving for Boston the next day".
questions.solution_en:
Option (c) is the correct answer.

The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· The reporting verb 'told' is changed into 'said to'.

· 'That' is replaced with inverted commas.

· The verb 'was leaving' (simple past continuous) is changed into 'am leaving' (simple present continuous).

· The pronoun 'she' is changed into 'I'.

· 'The next day' is changed into 'tomorrow'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): Brinda said to her doctor, "I am leaving for Boston tomorrow."

questions.q_en: Describe how you will say to your colleague You are wanted by the manager in active voice.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the verb 'are' and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Indefinite tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V1/V5 + Object.

For example:

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

She likes you. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.q_en:
Which of the following words has a similar meaning to the underlined word?

The salesman's glib answers to our questions made us suspicious about the product's actual quality.
questions.solution_en:
Glib - refers to words or a person speaking them that are fluent and voluble but insincere and shallow.

a) Gloomy - This means causing or feeling depression or despondency. It is unrelated to fluency.

b) Slick - This means done or operating in an impressively smooth and efficient way, but often superficially or deceitfully. This captures the fluency and insincerity of "glib."

c) Honest - This means free of deceit; truthful and sincere. It is an antonym of "glib".

d) Hesitant - This means tentative, unsure, or slow in acting or speaking. It is also an antonym of "glib".

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Last month, Ellen Konyak was shocked to discover that a 19th-century skull from the north-eastern Indian state of Nagaland was up for auction in the UK.

B. "To see that people are still auctioning our ancestral human remains in the 21st Century was shocking," she said.

C. The horned skull of a Naga tribesman was among thousands of items that European colonial administrators had collected from the state.

D. Konyak, a member of the Naga Forum for Reconciliation (NFR) which is making efforts to bring these human remains back home, says the news of the auction disturbed her.
questions.solution_en:
If the sentences are read carefully, it must be noted that sentence A is the starting point of the series of events that are mentioned in the sentences. So, it must be the first in the final order.

Sentence A is followed by C which talks about the stature of the auction and the other related things that were kept at the auction.

The pair AC is followed by D, in which the role that Konyak plays in retrieving the skull back to Nagaland and her feelings for the skull are mentioned. B sums it up. So, the final order is ACDB.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.solution_en:
Collocations are combinations of words that frequently occur together and have become established as natural expressions in a language. In this case, the verb "depend" is commonly used with the preposition "on" to indicate what something relies on. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The final sentence would be: The success of the project depends on your cooperation.
